category_title: Actively engaged students with severe disabilities in large-group instruction
minimal_context: The student is sitting on a small wooden chair on the carpet with peers, listening to the teacher read a story about the water cycle.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our group instruction. Please come to the carpet so I can read a story about the water cycle.

STUDENT: (Selects a fidget item from the bin and sits down in a small wooden chair on the carpet to be at the same level as the other students.)

TUTOR: I am going to start reading now. 'The sun warms the water in the ocean, and it turns into invisible vapor that floats up into the sky.'

STUDENT: (Sits on the carpet surrounded by peers, quietly listening to the teacher read the story.)

TUTOR: 'The vapor gets cold and turns into clouds.' What do you all think happens next?

STUDENT: (Exhibits passive engagement during the whole-group read-aloud activity, simply watching the teacher without responding to the question.)

options.A: Facilitate social interactions with peers, such as having a peer rub the back of the student.
options.B: Provide the student with a choice between two possible events that might happen next in the story.
options.C: Reread the relevant sentences in the story, ask the student to try again, and repeat the question.
options.D: When the student engages in passive behavior, do not provide them with any attention during the activity.
